question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom / Phrase.

To hit or miss the mark

options.text: To succeed or fail in an attempt
To speak a truth and lie at the same time
To retain one's position no matter what

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To hit or miss the mark"** means to either succeed or fail in an attempt. (सफलता या असफलता)

 
 
• **Example:** In business, you often **hit or miss the mark** depending on market conditions.
 
 
 
• **"To succeed or fail in an attempt"** refers to the outcome of an effort, where one can either achieve the desired result or not. (प्रयास में सफल या असफल होना)
 
 
• **Example:** His attempt to win the match could either** succeed or fail in an attempt.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning for the given idiom is **"To succeed or fail in an attempt."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To speak a truth and lie at the same time** (एक ही समय में सत्य और झूठ बोलना):

 
 
• **Example:** Politicians often **speak a truth and lie at the same time** to appeal to different voter bases.
 
 
 
• **To retain one's position no matter what** (चाहे कुछ भी हो अपनी स्थिति बनाए रखना):
 
 
• **Example:** Despite the controversies, he managed **to retain his position no matter what.**
 
 
 
• **To miss someone** (किसी को याद करना):
 
 
• **Example:** She began to **miss someone** as soon as she moved to a new city.
